desc: Design auxiliary graph with coordinate vertices: interval i connects to coord vertex L_i and R_i+1; verify shortest path in auxiliary graph equals shortest path in original (alternating real/coordinate, same weight sum).
Prove path correspondence: any path in original graph can be lifted to a path in auxiliary graph with same real-vertex weight sum, and vice versa.
Build auxiliary graph: O(N) vertices (~3N) and O(N) edges (~2N). Running Dijkstra per query is O(N log N), too slow for Q=2e5.
Recognize diameter is at most 3: shortest path between s and t is either direct edge, 2-hop (s-x-t), or 3-hop (s-x-y-t).
Handle direct edge: if R_s < L_t or R_t < L_s, answer = W_s + W_t.

Handle 2-hop: find min W_x where x is disjoint from both s and t. Reduce to min over intervals in coordinate ranges: left of min(L_s,L_t), right of max(R_s,R_t), and (if s,t disjoint) the gap between them. Preprocess prefix min by R and suffix min by L.

Handle 3-hop efficiently: enumerate cases based on relative positions of s and t, reduce each case to range-minimum queries over gaps using a segment tree built on array of (min W_x + W_y) for pairs straddling each gap.

Implement full solution: read input, sort intervals, preprocess prefix/suffix mins, build segment tree over gaps, answer each query in O(log N) by combining direct, 2-hop, and 3-hop candidates, print results.
Test on provided sample inputs and additional edge cases (e.g., all intervals identical, all intervals pairwise disjoint giving complete graph, N=2, overlapping/disjoint edge cases).
